title: Fill a cup at a lever soda fountain to just below the rim
instruction: Fill the paper cup with soda at the fountain, to about 1 cm below the rim, and set it down on the counter.
context: Fast food and counter workers (about 3.9 million in the US) fill fountain drinks for nearly every order: they hold the cup under the nozzle, keep its rim pressed against the sprung lever while it fills, and stop with room for the lid. Let go and the lever pushes the cup away; press off-centre and the drink runs onto the tray.
setup: Layout as in the screenshot (x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the left of the midline, heights from the counter). Dark grey laminate counter (50 x 80 x 0.3 cm) centred 34 cm out. Stainless steel single-valve soda fountain (10 cm deep, 24 cm wide, 32 cm tall), front face 50 cm out, centred 15 cm left, blue panel on its front. Steel valve head (6 x 8 x 5 cm, amber flavour badge) 18 to 23 cm up, centred 47 cm out; steel nozzle (2.4 cm across) at 43 cm out, 15 cm left, tip 16 cm up. Steel lever paddle (0.6 x 5 x 7 cm) hanging from a hinge 17.5 cm up, front face 45 cm out, sprung (about 4 N at the cup rim pushed 8 degrees; stops at 15); the drink runs while it is pushed in past 6 degrees. Steel drip tray with dark grate (14 x 20 x 1.2 cm) centred 45 cm out, 15 cm left. Empty paper cold cup with red stripes (6 cm across at the base, 9 cm at the rim, 11.6 cm tall, 30 g) upright 30 cm out, 15 cm left. Decor, fixed: a sleeve of spare paper cups (9 cm across, 20 cm tall) 40 cm out, 33 cm left; a stack of white plastic lids (9.4 cm across, 6 cm tall) 40 cm out, 10 cm right; a steel straw holder (6 cm across, 12 cm tall) with six white straws 47 cm out, 22 cm right; a steel napkin dispenser (8 x 12 x 9 cm) 50 cm out, 6 cm right.
scoring: 0 if the drink overflows the rim, more than 0.5 cm of drink level runs outside the cup (lever pushed with the cup's mouth more than 2.5 cm from the nozzle), or the cup tips more than 30 degrees. Otherwise 1.0 if the drink ends 0.5 to 2 cm below the rim with the cup set down upright (within 10 degrees) and still on the counter; 0.5 if the cup is at least half full and set down but the level is outside that band; else 0.
reset_notes: Empty and dry the cup (or use a new one) and wipe the drip tray.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, friction 1.2. Liquid is not simulated: while the lever is pushed in, the task file raises the drink level 1.6 cm a second if the cup's mouth is under the nozzle (else counts it as spilled) and draws it as cola layers in the cup; no foam. The lever is a sprung hinge; the cup is rigid and collides as a 7.6 cm cylinder inside its tapered wall. Real trials: a cold-drink or water paddle valve, level measured from the rim with a ruler.
